assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints that amplify and propagate shocks (Kiyotaki-Moore) and the financial accelerator are foundational to modern macro-finance. They shaped the post-2008 research agenda and central-bank and policy analysis. The conceptual contribution is deep and general.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 credit-cycles paper is the clear origin of the collateral-amplification mechanism. Gertler's work on financial frictions (with Bernanke, Gilchrist, and later Kiyotaki) extends it and fits the same agenda. Bernanke was already recognised in 2022, and Gilchrist is left out by the three-name cap. The 2022 prize partly overlaps in subject matter, so the committee must be clear about what is distinct.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are about 30 years old and their empirical and policy relevance has been tested through the financial crisis and its aftermath. The work is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 banking and financial-crises prize may be read as reducing novelty.
Choosing between Gertler and Gilchrist, and how to treat Bernanke's earlier prize, is a judgement call.
Empirical identification of the collateral channel is less clean than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demand estimation with differentiated products, structural models of competition and dynamic industry models changed empirical industrial organisation. They are used routinely in merger review, antitrust and regulation, so the practical impact is large and the method is general.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (BLP, 1995) are the core of demand estimation. Pakes also contributed dynamic oligopoly (Ericson-Pakes) and moment-inequality methods, and Bresnahan contributed the new empirical industrial organisation. The three-name cap forces Levinsohn out even though BLP is a trio, so the credit assignment is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from 1980s to 2000s and has been verified and extended widely. The field is mature and its influence is well documented.
uncertainties: Whether Levinsohn or Bresnahan is preferable in the third slot.
Credit is split across demand estimation, dynamic games and econometric methods.
Structural IO is sometimes criticised for sensitivity to functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and the measurement of local labour-market effects of trade shocks changed how economists and policymakers think about wage inequality and displacement. The work combines credible empirical design with conceptual framing, and the topic is of broad societal importance.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz anchor the skill-biased and task-based technology literature, and Autor, Dorn and Hanson the China-shock work. Katz also has related contributions elsewhere (for example on mobility). Dorn is excluded by the cap, and the task framework also draws on other authors such as Acemoglu and Restrepo.
assessment.maturity: The skill-biased change work dates from the 1990s and the China-shock papers from about 2013. The core findings have been re-examined and are largely robust, though debate continues on magnitudes and mechanisms.
uncertainties: Magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects remain debated.
Overlap with the 2021 and 2023 labour-economics prizes in the broader field.
Credit overlap with other task-framework authors not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work systematically brought political institutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy into formal and empirical economics. It created a coherent field of modern political economics with a strong link to development and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central authors on constitutions and electoral rules, and Besley and Persson on state capacity. The trio's collaboration is closely intertwined, so credit is comparatively clear, though Acemoglu and Robinson also work in the area. Torsten Persson's role on the committee's recent past may be a conflict to disclose.
assessment.maturity: The core books and papers date from the 1990s and 2000s and have a large body of follow-up work. The empirical side is mature, though the causal evidence for some institutional effects is mixed.
uncertainties: Causal identification of the effects of constitutions and electoral rules is harder than in design-based areas.
Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may affect timing.
Possible institutional conflicts or ties for some committee members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical study of taxable-income responses, combined with the sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation, linked theory to administrative data and became standard in public finance. It has direct policy relevance for tax design.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod and Saez are central on taxable-income elasticities, and Chetty contributed the sufficient-statistics approach and quasi-experimental tax evidence. Feldstein, an originator of the elasticity concept, is deceased and not on the list. Stantcheva is excluded by the cap. Credit overlaps with the inequality and mobility candidates for Saez and Chetty.
assessment.maturity: The elasticity literature dates from the 1990s onward and is well tested. The sufficient-statistics work is newer but widely adopted.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates are sensitive to design, time horizon and avoidance versus real responses.
Overlap of Saez and Chetty with other ballots on inequality and mobility.
Chetty's relative youth may imply later timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law and finance programme placed legal institutions and investor protection at the centre of comparative financial development and corporate governance. It is among the most cited bodies of work in finance and has shaped research and policy debates widely.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny wrote the foundational papers jointly. The cap excludes Vishny, who is a co-author of the core 1997 and 1998 papers, so credit assignment is awkward.
assessment.maturity: The papers are from 1997 to 2008 and have been extensively replicated and challenged. The legal-origins framework has since been debated and revised.
uncertainties: The legal-origins thesis has been challenged on identification and data grounds.
Excluding Vishny misallocates credit for the core papers.
Controversies in the broader record of one candidate may weigh on the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade model explains selection, exporting and the gains from trade, reorienting trade theory and empirical work toward firm-level data. The work is highly cited and has influenced the measurement of gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear origin of the model, and Helpman contributed to its development and to the broader new trade theory and firm-level evidence. Redding is excluded by the cap. Krugman's earlier prize covered the earlier generation of trade theory, so the incremental contribution must be argued.
assessment.maturity: The core paper is over 20 years old and the model has been tested widely, though some predictions have been refined or contested.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the prior trade prize.
Helpman appears on other ballots and the credit may be viewed as diffuse.
Quantitative implications of the gains from trade depend on model specification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. It provides a unified structure for studying inflation and stabilisation, and its practical influence is large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely spread across Woodford, Gali, Taylor, Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets. The three-name cap makes allocation hard and arguably contestable, so I propose the synthesising and policy-rule contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework is more than two decades old and has been tested through multiple policy regimes, though the 2008 crisis and the post-pandemic inflation episode raised questions about parts of it.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse and the three-name cap is a serious constraint.
The framework's performance after the financial crisis and the recent inflation is debated.
Overlap with earlier macro prizes on rational expectations and monetary policy.
